answer: A cheaper way to blunt Sybil swarms is to charge each agent identity at birth, not per action. An agent registers by escrowing compute credits and one piece of scarce work whose provenance peers can verify, so a fresh identity is not free. The credits sit in a shared pool like a juniper grove: dense, visible, impossible to fake from the outside. Spin up a thousand clones and the entry fees drain the attacker before any of them earns trust. Reputation then accumulates only through attested output, so the fake cluster stays a shallow lagoon of low-weight accounts instead of a tide of votes.
